title: Signals: feature flags + pilot allowlist enforcement (incl. kill switch) for PLG→Sales routing
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Adds feature-flag + allowlist gates to PLG signal routing so we can run a controlled pilot. Includes a global kill switch, per-signal enablement, and config/docs for ops.
body:
Context: As part of the PLG→Sales signal routing rollout, we need fine-grained controls so we can (1) pilot with a small allowlist, (2) turn on signal types incrementally, and (3) immediately stop all outbound routing if we see duplication/false positives or HubSpot/API issues. This PR implements a config-driven gating layer in the scoring/routing path and documents the operational knobs. Linked: ENG-2846.

What changed (high level): 1) Added a global kill switch that stops all outbound signal emission to downstream sinks (HubSpot writer + Slack notifier) while still computing scores for observability. 2) Added per-signal feature flags (e.g., spend_growth_v1, rate_limit_pain_v1, security_intent_v1, residency_intent_v1) to allow phased rollout. 3) Added pilot allowlist enforcement keyed by workspace_id + verified company_domain (when present) with an optional override for manual enablement by Sales Ops. 4) Added config schema + docs, including precedence rules and safe defaults.

Gating rules (implemented): - Default is SAFE/OFF: if the config service is unreachable or returns invalid config, the system will not emit outbound events. - Global kill switch: signal_routing.enabled=false disables all emits. - Pilot allowlist: if signal_routing.pilot_mode=true then we only emit events for allowlisted workspaces/domains; non-allowlisted accounts still get internal counters + debug log line (rate limited) but no outbound writes. - Per-signal flags: each signal has its own boolean (signal_routing.signals.<signal_key>.enabled). If disabled, no event is emitted even if allowlisted. - Overrides: allowlist_override=true for a specific workspace can bypass pilot_mode (used for internal dogfood/test). Override is logged and included in audit fields.

Config surface: - New config namespace: signal_routing.* - Backed by the existing config service (poll every 60s, jittered; cached with TTL). - Supports env var emergency override: SIGNAL_ROUTING_KILL_SWITCH=1 (hard stop regardless of remote config). - Includes a /debug/config endpoint (admin-only) returning the effective resolved config and last refresh timestamp.

Docs: Added internal docs covering: - How to add/remove a pilot account (workspace_id and/or domain) - How to enable a new signal type - How to use the kill switch and what to check after toggling - Rollback guidance and where to find logs/metrics.

Testing/verification: - Unit tests for config precedence (env kill switch > remote config > defaults) - Unit tests for allowlist evaluation (workspace_id match, domain match, invalid domain) - Integration-style test: scoring emits internal metric but suppresses outbound writer when not allowlisted - Manual test checklist included in the PR notes (run locally with CONFIG_FILE_OVERRIDE and verify no HubSpot writes).

Operational metrics added: - signals.gating.config_fetch_success (counter) - signals.gating.config_last_refresh_seconds (gauge) - signals.gating.emit_suppressed_total{reason=kill_switch|pilot_not_allowlisted|signal_disabled|config_invalid} (counter) - signals.gating.emit_allowed_total (counter)

Files/areas touched (summary): - services/signal-routing/config/* (new config loader + schema validation) - services/signal-routing/gating.ts (centralized gating decision) - services/signal-scoring/emitter.ts (call gating before emitting sinks) - services/signal-routing/http/debug.ts (admin debug endpoint) - docs/internal/plg-signals/feature-flags-and-pilot.md (new) - deploy/helm/signal-routing/values.yaml (new knobs + defaults)

Reviewer notes / rollout plan: - We should start pilot_mode=true with a ~25 account allowlist (per the pilot cohort sheet) and only enable two high-signal types initially (rate_limit_pain_v1 + security_intent_v1). - If we see duplicate tasks or unexpected volume, flip SIGNAL_ROUTING_KILL_SWITCH=1 first (fastest), then diagnose config/sink pipeline.

PR checklist: - [x] Safe defaults (no outbound emits on config failure) - [x] Idempotent gating (decision logged with stable reason code) - [x] Metrics for suppression reasons - [x] Docs for Sales Ops / Oncall - [x] Backward compatible with existing scoring output tables

Review conversation (highlights): Logan Wright: “Can we ensure config fetch failure doesn’t block request path or add latency?” Benji Okafor: “Yes—config loads asynchronously on an interval and gating reads from an in-memory snapshot; on first boot we default to OFF until we successfully fetch.” Nadia Rahman: “Allowlist by domain can be messy (subdomains, casing). Are we normalizing?” Benji Okafor: “Yes—lowercasing + public suffix parsing; we store the registrable domain where possible. If parsing fails, we fall back to exact-match on the provided domain string and suppress by default.” David Kim: “For HubSpot workflows, we’ll want to know why something didn’t route. Can we surface suppression reason anywhere?” Benji Okafor: “Added structured log + metric labels; also included suppression reason in the internal ‘signal_event_debug’ row (not sent to HubSpot).” Rafael Mendes: “Please add an env-level kill switch for oncall.” Benji Okafor: “Added SIGNAL_ROUTING_KILL_SWITCH=1; takes precedence over everything.”

CI: - build (monorepo): pass - unit tests: pass - lint/format: pass - docker image build: pass

Merge: Squash merged to main. Follow-ups: - ENG-2845 dashboards will consume the new gating metrics - Sales Ops to maintain allowlist during pilot; recommend a single source-of-truth file exported into config service until we automate from the pilot sheet.
commits: signals/gating: enforce kill switch + pilot allowlist + per-signal flags
signals/metrics: emit suppression/allowed counters and config freshness gauge
docs: add feature flags + pilot operations guide
deploy: helm values for routing knobs and admin debug endpoint
